verdict.rationale: Stripe's own docs say Terminal supports an API-based integration alongside its SDKs for building a custom POS. They also name a 'server-driven integration' that includes a simulated reader for testing. A community developer separately praises the ability to integrate with the API at the terminal level. Missing for 10: endpoint-level documentation of how the backend drives the reader (e.g., sending a payment to the reader, cancelling, showing cart or display), and hands-on corroboration of a full server-driven checkout flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom point-of-sale checkout that drives the terminal from my backend through a documented server-driven API

citations.quote: Build a custom POS integration tailored to your business. Terminal supports an API-based integration in addition to SDKs for Android, iOS, JavaScript, and React Native.
Stripe Terminal SDKs and server-driven integration come with a built-in simulated card reader, so you can develop and test your app without connecting to physical hardware.
the ability to fully integrate with the API on a terminal level is the most powerful thing here
